newsitem.title: UK: Saab AB sees common European future.
newsitem.headline: Saab AB sees common European future.

text.p: The chief executive of Swedish civil and military aerospace group Saab AB said on Tuesday that, like its UK partner British Aerospace Plc, the firm sees its future firmly within common European production projects.
BAe has used the ocassion of the Farnborough airshow this week to reveal its idea of "dissolving into Europe", expecting all its activities to fall into multinational ventures.
"We have a vision very close to that of BAe. When we have talk to their management we are very much in agreement," chief executive Bengt Halse told Reuters here.
At Farnborough, Saab and BAe have rolled out their international marketing coperation plan based around the new Saab Gripen, now in service with the Swedish Air Force.

BAe is also forging manufacturing links with Saab on the Gripen programme, to help reduce its production costs, and executives expect there could be opportunities for Saab to recoup some work by subcontracting for Eurofighter, even though the company is not within this four-nation alliance.

Halse predicted that the next miltary aircraft programme in Europe "will have to be done in parallel", and by that he said he meant that Eurofighter, Gripen and Dassault's new Rafale should be superceded by one jointly developed range.

"We have to endeavour to get a single European programme," he added. Eurofighter's partners at present are BAe, with the largest share of the proposed production work, Daimler Aerospace, Italy's Alenia and CASA of Spain.
The British company has also forged research and development links with France's Dassault in preparation for future military aircraft programmes.
Saab is also drawn closer to Europe's commercial airliner cooperative Airbus Industries through its links with British Aerospace, which has a central role in that grouping, too.
Halse said there was also a likelihood, though it would take time, that Saab would integrate its commercial aerospace activity into the Airbus structure.

He said the company was glad to be in discussion with Airbus as a possible partner in the development of the proposed A3XX super-jumbo, but he said it was too early to predict what areas of technology or expertise Saab might contribute.

Looking at the likely obstacles ahead of the closer integration of Europe's manufacturers in this key strategic industry, Halse said he had no illusions about the political and commerical complexities of creating closer-knit ventures.
Echoing recent comments by Manfred Bischoff, head of Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Halse said the different interests of privately-owned and state-backed companies would need to be balanced with care.
"Just like BAe, we don't have any money other than our shaeholders' funds," he said.
